To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the retina is a complex organ that expresses thousands of genes and that the expression of these genes is regulated in a cell-specific and developmental manner.

1) the retina expresses a large number of genes, many of which are not found in other tissues; 2) the expression pattern of many genes in the retina is restricted to subsets of cells; 3) genes expressed in the mouse retina are evolutionarily conserved; 4) the retina expresses many genes that are not expressed in other tissues; and 5) many genes expressed in the mammalian retina are expressed in the retina of the chicken.
we identified genes that are differentially expressed in the retina and are involved in visual transduction, neuronal function and disease.

the identification, characterization and analysis of genes expressed in retinal neurons.
the molecular basis of retinal development and disease, and is focused on the identification and characterization of genes that are expressed in the retina.
